item.title: ROKI Pure Brings a Deeper Approach to Wellness to Queenstown
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
ROKI Pure, the wellness sanctuary at ROKI Collection Queenstown on the shores of Lake Wakatipu, has been named New Zealand’s Best Hotel Spa 2026 by the World Spa Awards. The recognition comes in the sanctuary’s first year and reflects an approach to wellness built around moving beyond conventional relaxation. Its treatments, known as Rituals, are designed as extended journeys of two hours or more, incorporating elements such as infrared blankets, tuning forks, magnesium-infused scrubs and sensory-focused products to encourage a calmer, more restorative state.

Wellness at ROKI extends beyond the treatment rooms. Guests can use the heated indoor pool, jacuzzi, thermal suites, cold plunges, traditional saunas and fitness room, while the broader program includes self-led in-suite Resets, nature-based Rewild experiences and a personalized Sleep Concierge. The setting adds another dimension, with Queenstown’s mountains, lake and outdoor environment becoming part of the experience rather than simply a backdrop to the spa.

The Curated Take: ROKI Pure is part of a broader evolution in destination wellness toward experiences that are less about pampering and more about changing how a traveler feels. The combination of longer treatments, sensory rituals, sleep support and time in nature gives the spa a distinctly place-based approach, particularly suited to Queenstown, where an active outdoor destination can naturally be paired with deeper recovery.

item.title: Coastal Mississippi Turns the Gulf Coast Into Halloween Country
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Coastal Mississippi is trading beach days for haunted nights this October, with Halloween celebrations stretching across 62 miles of Gulf Coast from Gulfport and Biloxi to Ocean Springs and Bay St. Louis. The season ranges from the elaborate sets and live actors of Terror on the Coast, a 40,000-square-foot haunted attraction in Gulfport, to family-friendly festivals, costume parades and community celebrations. The result is a distinctly coastal take on Halloween, with historic downtowns, beaches and waterfront communities providing the setting rather than a traditional theme-park backdrop.

The calendar also offers reasons to experience the Coast after dark in less expected ways. Ocean Springs hosts a candlelit string quartet performing Halloween film scores, while its Witches Ride brings hundreds of costumed participants through downtown in support of local animal welfare organizations. Bay St. Louis turns its historic Old Town into the setting for a Witches Walk, and Biloxi adds live music and cultural events, including the Moonlight Masquerade and a performance by Here Come the Mummies. For families, Boo Bash, Fall Fest and Brick or Treat at TrainTastic provide gentler ways to join the season.

The Curated Take: Coastal Mississippi’s Halloween appeal comes from the way the celebrations are woven into the destination’s individual communities. Rather than one large seasonal attraction, visitors can move between historic districts, beach towns, music venues and local festivals, experiencing different sides of the Gulf Coast along the way. Halloween becomes an excuse to explore the region, with seafood, arts, shoreline and Southern hospitality providing the backdrop between events.

item.title: Four Seasons Singapore Extends Its MICHELIN Key Run
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Four Seasons Hotel Singapore has retained its One MICHELIN Key for a second consecutive year, continuing its recognition for a style of hospitality built around personalized service, thoughtful design and a strong connection to place. Set along tree-lined Orchard Boulevard, the hotel offers a quieter counterpoint to Singapore’s urban energy, with accommodation, dining and wellness experiences designed around both privacy and connection. The latest addition is a 180-square-metre Three-Bedroom Premier Suite, giving families and groups a spacious setting to gather while maintaining separate spaces to retreat.

That balance extends throughout the property. MICHELIN-selected Jiang-Nan Chun presents refined Cantonese cuisine, while Nobu Singapore brings Japanese-Peruvian flavors and One-Ninety takes a more botanical approach to dining. The Four Seasons Spa and Chi Longevity Clinic add a wellness dimension, from restorative treatments to science-led health and longevity programs. Together, the experiences reflect the hotel’s emphasis on anticipating individual needs rather than treating luxury as a purely material experience.

The Curated Take: The MICHELIN Key recognition is most meaningful here as an acknowledgment of the details behind an urban hotel stay. In a city as dynamic as Singapore, Four Seasons creates its distinction through the quieter elements: intuitive service, generous private space, thoughtful dining and opportunities to slow down. It is a model of city luxury that places the quality of the experience ahead of spectacle.

item.title: One Island, Two MICHELIN Keys, and Two Ways to Experience the Whitsundays
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Hamilton Island has become home to two MICHELIN Key hotels, giving the small Whitsunday island an unusual concentration of internationally recognized stays. Adults-only qualia has retained its MICHELIN Key for a second consecutive year, while The Sundays, a 59-room boutique hotel that opened in 2025, has received its first. The distinction recognizes hotels for qualities including design, service, character, value and connection to place, and in Hamilton Island’s case, the two properties offer distinctly different interpretations of island hospitality.

At qualia, privacy, personalized service and access to the natural environment remain central, with experiences extending from Pebble Beach dining and wellness to private excursions around Whitehaven Beach, Heart Island and the Great Barrier Reef. The Sundays takes a more social, family-focused approach, with its Catseye Beach setting, waterside pool and Catseye Pool Club, the restaurant from Australian chefs Josh and Julie Niland. Together, the properties reflect the broader evolution of Hamilton Island, where luxury is increasingly expressed through different kinds of experiences rather than a single resort model.

The Curated Take: The more interesting story here is not simply that Hamilton Island has two MICHELIN Keys. It is that one destination can accommodate two very different versions of the Australian island escape. qualia is built around seclusion and refinement, while The Sundays makes togetherness and family time part of the experience. Both ultimately draw their character from the same setting: the Whitsundays and the extraordinary waters of the Great Barrier Reef.

item.title: Five Islands, Five Ways to Celebrate the Festive Season in the Maldives
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The festive season takes on a different rhythm in the Maldives, where celebration unfolds between ocean, shore and the distinctive character of each island. This year, five Marriott International luxury resorts are approaching the holidays through different lenses, from contemporary art and marine discovery to Maldivian heritage, wellness and lively celebrations. Together, The Ritz-Carlton Maldives, Fari Islands, JW Marriott Maldives Kaafu Atoll Island Resort, The St. Regis Maldives Vommuli Resort, W Maldives and JW Marriott Maldives Resort & Spa offer contrasting ways for families, couples and friends to spend the season together.

At The Ritz-Carlton Maldives, festive programming brings French artist Alexandre Benjamin Navet’s colorful work to the island, while nearby JW Marriott Maldives Kaafu Atoll focuses on family time, wellness and lagoon adventures. Farther into the archipelago, The St. Regis Maldives Vommuli Resort celebrates its 10th anniversary through the island’s ecological zones and Maldivian fishing and seafaring heritage. W Maldives takes a more energetic approach with music, nightlife and access to its house reef and private island, while JW Marriott Maldives Resort & Spa in Shaviyani Atoll combines spacious villas, marine experiences, family programming and evening performances. The journeys themselves, whether by speedboat or seaplane, become part of the transition from Malé into a slower island world.

The Curated Take: What makes the Maldives particularly compelling for the festive season is the ability to choose the atmosphere rather than simply the setting. One island can turn the holidays into an art-filled escape, another into a multigenerational gathering, another into a celebration of local ecology and heritage. The common thread is time together, with the ocean providing the backdrop and each island supplying its own interpretation of what a holiday escape can be.

item.title: Orlando’s Fall Calendar Goes Well Beyond the Theme Parks
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Orlando’s fall calendar is making the destination relevant to travelers for reasons that extend well beyond its famous theme parks. From the Southern Hill Farms Fall Festival and Winter Park Autumn Art Festival to the Central Florida Veg Fest, EPCOT International Food & Wine Festival and Swan and Dolphin Food & Wine Classic, autumn brings a diverse mix of food, art, seasonal traditions and cultural celebrations. The city’s 94-day Halloween season adds another layer, while events such as FusionFest and Fiesta Calle Orange reflect the many cultures that shape Central Florida.

Music and sports give fall travelers another reason to build a trip around a particular date. Electric Daisy Carnival returns to Tinker Field, the Vans Warped Tour brings punk, alternative and emo music to Camping World Stadium, and concerts by artists including Doja Cat, Olivia Rodrigo and SOMBR add major touring acts to the calendar. Meanwhile, the Orlando Magic, Orlando Solar Bears, Orlando City SC and Orlando Pride offer professional basketball, hockey and soccer. Even the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex joins the culinary calendar with Taste of Space: Fall Bites!, adding a distinctly Central Florida twist to the season.

The Curated Take: Orlando’s fall appeal is increasingly about choosing your own reason to go. A traveler might come for a food festival, an art weekend, a major concert, a soccer match or Halloween, with the city’s broader dining, entertainment and cultural landscape filling in the itinerary. That makes fall less a single Orlando experience and more a collection of distinct ways to experience the destination.

item.title: The Laurel Highlands Makes Fall Foliage a Destination
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Pennsylvania’s Laurel Highlands has earned a place among the country’s standout fall foliage destinations for the seventh consecutive year, placing sixth in the 2026 USA Today 10Best Readers’ Choice Awards for Best Destination for Fall Colors. Set across the Allegheny Mountains, the region typically reaches peak color around mid-October, when its mountain ridges and river valleys take on layers of red, gold, and orange. Nearly 200,000 acres of public lands, along with hiking and biking trails including the Great Allegheny Passage, give visitors plenty of ways to experience the landscape beyond a scenic drive.

The season also brings a distinctly local rhythm to the Laurel Highlands, with festivals and attractions providing reasons to linger. Confluence PumpkinFest, Fort Ligonier Days, Delmont Apple ‘n Arts Festival, and Seven Springs Autumnfest fill the September and October calendar, while the region’s historic sites and architectural landmarks offer another dimension to an autumn visit. Fallingwater, Kentuck Knob, and other Frank Lloyd Wright works, along with Ohiopyle State Park and the area’s mountain resorts, make the foliage backdrop part of a broader cultural and outdoor itinerary.

The Curated Take: The Laurel Highlands is most interesting in fall when the foliage becomes a gateway rather than the entire experience. The combination of mountain landscapes, Frank Lloyd Wright architecture, historic sites, local festivals, craft beverages, and outdoor recreation gives visitors reasons to build an itinerary around the season rather than simply pass through in search of peak color.

item.title: Rethinking What It Means to Age Well in the Texas Hill Country
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Lake Austin Spa Resort is bringing together women working across wellness, healthcare and spa leadership for Better with Age: Women Redefining Longevity, Leadership & Wellbeing on October 14 and 15. Created in partnership with Glowing Older and hosted by its founder, Nancy Griffin, the gathering will explore longevity, women’s health, purpose and wellbeing as part of Lake Austin’s monthlong A Gathering of W.I.S.E. Women series. Speakers include wellness executive Laura Gamboa, Northwestern University professor Dr. Ruchi Gupta and author Susan Salenger, alongside an interactive session focused on personal values.

The program reflects a broader shift in how wellness is approaching aging, moving beyond appearance and conventional anti-aging narratives toward health, purpose, connection and quality of life. Day guests will also have access to Lake Austin’s all-inclusive resort experience, including lunch, spa treatments, wellness programming and lake activities, creating space to consider those ideas within a broader retreat setting.

The Curated Take: The most compelling aspect of Better with Age is its premise that aging well is not simply a matter of extending life, but of considering how we want to live it. Bringing conversations about women’s health, leadership, personal values and longevity into a destination wellness setting makes the retreat part of a larger cultural conversation about what wellbeing looks like across different stages of life.

item.title: Tualatin Valley Finds New Flavors for Fall
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Just 20 minutes from Portland, Oregon, Tualatin Valley offers a gateway into the northern reaches of Willamette Valley wine country, where vineyards and farms increasingly intersect with an ambitious culinary scene. This fall brings several new ways to experience that connection, including Sazanami, a 14-seat, adults-only omakase restaurant from James Beard Award-winning chef Hajime Sato. Opened in July, the nine-course experience changes with the day’s freshest ingredients and emphasizes sustainably sourced seafood, giving Beaverton an intimate destination for serious sushi without a trip into downtown Portland.

The season also brings new ways to experience Oregon’s agricultural bounty. At Ponzi Vineyards, The Laurelwood Table pairs a four-course lunch from chef Eric Ekberg with the estate’s single-vineyard wines, while the Women’s Adventure Weekend Harvest Weekend in October brings together wine, hazelnuts, saké, chocolate making and peak-season produce through a hands-on three-day retreat. Together, the additions highlight a side of the Willamette Valley that is as much about meeting the people, producers and chefs behind the region’s food as it is about tasting the finished product.

The Curated Take: Tualatin Valley’s appeal is increasingly found in the space between city and wine country. Its proximity to Portland makes it easy to reach, but the combination of estate vineyards, agricultural producers and destination-worthy dining gives travelers reasons to slow down and explore beyond the usual Willamette Valley itinerary.

item.title: When Soccer Fandom Becomes a Reason to Travel
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
For millions of soccer fans, following a club is about far more than the 90 minutes on the pitch. New research commissioned by G Adventures for the launch of its Away Games small-group sports travel series suggests that soccer fandom can shape identity, friendships and even travel decisions, with nearly 70 percent of respondents saying the sport gives them a sense of belonging and makes them feel less lonely. Three-quarters have made friends with strangers through soccer, while 64 percent say they would travel with a group of people they had never met if they supported the same club.

That sense of community is increasingly extending beyond home stadiums. The research found that 69 percent of fans said the 2026 World Cup increased their desire to travel internationally for soccer, but overseas match trips can come with their own anxieties. Fake tickets, language barriers, unfamiliar transit systems and the possibility of ending up among rival supporters all ranked among fans’ concerns. Away Games is designed around those friction points, combining guaranteed premium or VIP match tickets with small-group itineraries led by locally based, soccer-focused Chief Experience Officers.

The new trips span some of Europe’s great soccer cities, including Madrid, London, Barcelona and Manchester. Experiences pair major club matches with the culture surrounding them, from local supporter pubs and lower-league terrace matches to tapas tours, food markets, neighborhood explorations and city history. The lineup includes itineraries centered on Real Madrid, Arsenal, Chelsea, FC Barcelona, Manchester City and Manchester United, creating a way for travelers to experience both the spectacle of elite soccer and the communities that surround it.

The Curated Take: The most interesting element of Away Games is the decision to treat soccer as a gateway into a city rather than the sole purpose of the trip. The stadium may be the anchor, but the stronger travel experience is in understanding what a club means to its supporters, where they gather, what they eat and how the sport fits into local identity. For travelers who already see soccer as part of their cultural world, this approach turns fandom into a distinctly social form of travel.
